**About Anthropic**
-------------------

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

**About the role**
------------------

Anthropic's Life Sciences team is building a research group focused on biological discoveries by combining AI with hands-on biological research. We're seeking a research scientist with deep expertise in therapeutic antibodies to join the team. Our goal is to speed up progress in the life sciences by an order of magnitude, and this role puts that mission into practice. You'll be an expert in antibody design and engineering who has taken antibodies through the whole process, from target selection and lead optimization to candidate selection and IND-enabling studies. Above all, you'll close the loop between AI-generated hypotheses and experimental data to share with the community. Working alongside AI researchers and engineers, you'll drive antibody programs end to end and pressure-test AI-designed antibodies against the bar a real drug candidate has to clear.

This role is fully on-site in the San Francisco Bay Area.

**Key responsibilities**
------------------------

* Design and engineer therapeutic antibodies and oversee programs end to end, including target and epitope selection, choice of format (IgG, Fab, scFv, VHH, bispecific), humanization, affinity maturation, Fc engineering, and candidate selection
* Define the screening cascade for each program, from binding kinetics (SPR, BLI), epitope binning, and species cross-reactivity to cell-based functional assays and developability (expression, aggregation, polyreactivity, stability, viscosity, immunogenicity risk)
* Plan the path from lead to IND-enabling studies, including in vivo pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, toxicology, and the handoff to process development and manufacturing
* Coordinate antibody production, characterization, and in vitro and in vivo studies with external contract research organizations and academic partners

* Comfort navigating ambiguity and defining problems in a rapidly evolving research environment
* Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across cross-functional teams, with strong written and verbal communication skills

* Track record of advancing more than one antibody program into IND-enabling studies or the clinic, with contributions to pre-IND or IND documents

* Structural biology, computational protein design, or coding skills, for example Python for sequence and assay data analysis or structure prediction and protein design tools
* Experience using AI or ML tools in the life sciences

jobs.title: Senior Engineer, Bioinformatics
jobs.description:
**About Anthropic**
-------------------

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

**About the role**
------------------

As a Senior Software Engineer on the Life Sciences team, you'll build biology software that our own scientists and the wider research community can depend on, and you'll be one of the main people representing that work to computational biologists outside Anthropic.

The Life Sciences team works to accelerate progress in biology with AI, combining frontier models with hands-on computational and experimental research. We want the tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks we build in genomics and structural biology to be useful beyond our own projects, so we plan to release them to the community. Computational biology has a long tradition of open, shared software, and we want to contribute to it well. Every release should be something a researcher can install, run on their own data, and trust: correct on real inputs, validated against reference data and established methods, documented, versioned, and maintained after launch.

You'll own that standard. You'll write a large share of the code yourself, decide when something is ready to ship, and stay with it once people start using it. You'll also be an active member of the biology software community: maintaining public repositories, answering issues, speaking at conferences and workshops, and bringing what you hear from researchers back into what we build next.

We use Claude and AI coding agents heavily to build software, and we expect you to do the same across design, implementation, testing, and review. Code written by an agent is held to the same standard as code written by hand: you should understand it, test it, and measure its performance before it ships. We're looking for someone with deep software engineering experience who already works this way.

The shape of the role is flexible. You might spend most of your time as an individual contributor, or you might lead a small group of engineers and scientists while continuing to contribute directly. Your focus can be genomics, structural biology, or both. Experience in other areas of computational biology is welcome, and we expect the work to range more widely over time.

What matters most is a record of biology software that other people have adopted and relied on.

This is a chance to shape how AI is put to work in biological research, on problems that matter for human health and scientific understanding. If building software that scientists trust is the work you want to do, we want to hear from you.

**Key responsibilities**
------------------------

* Design, build, and maintain biology software in genomics and structural biology (libraries, command-line tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks) for use by researchers and AI agents, inside Anthropic and externally
* Own the path from research code to public release, including testing, validation against reference data and established tools, benchmarking, documentation, and packaging, and make the call on when something is ready to ship
* Maintain what we release: triage issues, review outside contributions, and manage breaking changes
* Represent the team in the biology community through conferences, workshops, tutorials, and direct work with researchers and maintainers, and turn what you learn about their needs into priorities for the team
* Partner with the team's computational and experimental scientists to turn research code into well-tested, reusable software
* Lead the technical direction of the projects you own through design review, code review, and mentoring, and, depending on your interests and the team's needs, lead a small team
* Build with Claude and AI coding agents as your default way of working, hold agent-written code to the same standard as your own, and set the team's practices for reviewing and validating it

**Minimum qualifications**
--------------------------

* Have built, released, and maintained biology software that researchers outside your own group use, with evidence of adoption you can point to (for example public repositories, package downloads, citations, or use in other groups' pipelines)
* Have deep working expertise in genomics or structural biology, including the data types, file formats, standard tools, and common failure modes of at least one of these fields
* Are proficient in Python and comfortable working with large datasets in Linux and cloud or cluster computing environments
* Practice rigorous testing and release engineering: unit and integration tests, continuous integration, validation against reference data, packaging, and versioning
* Use AI coding tools as a central part of how you build software, and can show how you verify the correctness and performance of code you did not write by hand
* Have led a technical project with multiple contributors, setting direction and reviewing others' work while continuing to write code yourself
* Can explain technical work clearly to both biologists and engineers, in writing (documentation, tutorials) and in person (talks, workshops)

**Preferred qualifications**
----------------------------

* Depth in both genomics and structural biology
* A record as the creator or a core maintainer of a widely used open-source tool in computational biology
* Experience managing or formally leading a team of engineers or scientists
* A graduate degree in computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent experience

new_jobs.description:
**Department:**

R&D

  

**Location:**

Irvine, CA

  

**Job Summary:**

Zymo Research is seeking a Research Associate to join the Epigenetics Technology group and support next-generation sequencing (NGS) assay development for DNA methylation and cancer research, including probe enrichment and library preparation for methylation and genetic variant analysis.

Working with project scientists, the associate will apply molecular biology and enzymatic techniques to feasibility studies, optimization, and validation using cell-free DNA (cfDNA), formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue DNA, and reference materials.

Join us in making a meaningful impact!

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* Execute planned experiments for probe enrichment, DNA methylation, and cancer assay development (variants/SNPs). Prepare reagents and controls and contribute to experimental planning and troubleshooting with project scientists.
* Perform and optimize probe enrichment assays, including hybridization, capture, washing, recovery, and amplification as applicable. Assess enrichment efficiency, specificity, reproducibility, and recovery.
* Prepare NGS libraries using enzymatic processing, adapter incorporation, amplification, and purification. Measure DNA concentration, fragment size, and library yield; investigate artifacts and failed reactions.
* Perform end point PCR, qPCR/ddPCR, and other quantitative assays to assess DNA quality, enrichment, conversion, and recovery. Support primer and probe evaluation.
* Conduct enzyme-based experiments using polymerases, ligases, nucleases, and other nucleic acid-modifying enzymes. Vary conditions systematically and record results to support optimization.
* Process low-input samples with careful tracking and contamination control. Support validation using methylation and variant/SNPs standards, defined mixtures, and appropriate cancer and non-cancer specimens.
* Maintain complete laboratory records, summarize results, and flag unexpected findings. Help update SOPs, manage reagents and inventory, and contribute to other projects requiring relevant skills.

**Supervisory Responsibilities and Core Competencies**

* No formal supervisory responsibilities. May help train colleagues on established procedures once proficient. Key competencies include accuracy, reproducibility, organization, practical problem-solving, clear communication, and teamwork.

**Education and Experience**

* Master/Bachelor’s degree in molecular biology, biochemistry, genetics, biotechnology, or a related field, with relevant hands-on laboratory experience.
* Demonstrated experience performing NGS library preparation and probe-based target enrichment assays, including routine optimization, quality control, and troubleshooting.
* Ability to execute multi-step protocols accurately, organize experiments, and maintain traceable laboratory records.

**Required Scientific and Technical Skills**

* Strong practical molecular biology skills, including nucleic acid handling (DNA/RNA), accurate pipetting, PCR and qPCR, enzymatic reactions, purification, and DNA and library quality control.
* Working knowledge of enzymology and the effects of enzyme concentration, substrate quality, incubation conditions, titrations, and buffer composition on assay performance.
* Ability to perform and troubleshoot probe-based target enrichment workflows and understand how hybridization conditions, washing, and amplification affect recovery and specificity.
* Ability to analyze experimental results using spreadsheets and basic statistics, summarize data clearly, and communicate with scientists and bioinformatics colleagues.
* Attention to detail, reliable sample and reagent management, good laboratory practices, and the ability to manage several experiments and priorities with appropriate guidance.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with DNA methylation assays, bisulfite/enzymatic conversion chemistry, cancer research, low-input cfDNA or FFPE samples, and exome capture.
* Experience with digital PCR, UMI-based libraries, automated liquid handling, or assay transfer into routine workflows.
* Experience supporting NGS methods development, evaluating enzyme performance, or interpreting sequencing quality metrics such as on-target fraction, coverage, duplication, and conversion efficiency.
  

**About Us:**

Since its inception in 1994, Zymo Research has been proudly serving the scientific community by providing innovative, reliable, and high-quality research tools and products. Whether it's DNA, RNA, epigenetics, microbiomics, protein, or yeast-based research, our philosophy remains the same: To provide the highest quality products in the industry while ensuring they are both simple to use and reliable in their performance.

Recognized as a *Top Workplace* by the Orange County Register in 2021, 2022, and named a *Top Workplace USA* in 2023, Zymo Research continues to be a vibrant community where employees thrive, feel connected, and are inspired by their work.
